outline: 643 Area of Composite Figures with Special Quadrilaterals

examples.solution_text:
The parallel sides are $6\text{ cm}$ and $11\text{ cm}$. The perpendicular height is $4.5\text{ cm}$.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\&=\frac{4.5(6+11)}{2}\\&=\frac{4.5\times17}{2}\\&=38.25\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

The arrow marks identify the vertical parallel sides: $a=8\text{ cm}$ and $b=4\text{ cm}$. The top side meets both at right angles, so $h=6\text{ cm}$. The sloping side is not the height.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\&=\frac{6(8+4)}{2}\\&=\frac{6\times12}{2}\\&=36\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

Convert the parallel sides to the same unit before substituting.

$280\text{ cm}=2.8\text{ m}$

The arrow-marked sides are parallel. The right-angle mark identifies the perpendicular height, $1.8\text{ m}$.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\&=\frac{1.8(1.2+2.8)}{2}\\&=\frac{1.8\times4}{2}\\&=3.6\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A trapezium has a shorter parallel side of $7\text{ cm}$. Its longer parallel side is $5\text{ cm}$ longer, and its perpendicular height is $4\text{ cm}$. Find its area.
examples.solution_text:
Find the longer parallel side first.

$\begin{aligned}b&=7+5\\&=12\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{h(a+b)}{2}\\&=\frac{4(7+12)}{2}\\&=\frac{4\times19}{2}\\&=38\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$
